title: Aligning to objectives: benefits and sustainability tolerances, ESG
blurb: Explain how the business case aligns to business objectives and ESG goals, and where benefits and sustainability targets and tolerances are documented.
question: An organization has committed to cutting its carbon emissions. A project sets a carbon target with a permitted margin. Where should that target and margin be documented?

teach.h: Products must serve the business's objectives
teach.body: Formally: the outcomes and benefits the project achieves must align with, and contribute to, the business objectives, and those objectives may include environmental, social and governance (ESG) goals set by the organization. Targets and tolerances make that alignment measurable. In plain English: it is not enough to build the right things; the results must move the organization's goals forward, including its promises on the environment and society.

Benefits tolerance is the permissible deviation in the benefit performance targets before the deviation must be escalated to the next level of management: how far benefits may be under- or over-delivered. It is documented in the benefits management approach, alongside how and when benefits will be measured and reviewed.

Sustainability is the seventh aspect of performance. Sustainability tolerance sets limits on agreed sustainability metrics, such as carbon or waste. The project's sustainability performance targets and tolerances are documented in the sustainability management approach, which supports the business case and should reference, and contribute to, the organization's ESG goals.

teach.caption: Benefits and quality tolerances are not agreed in a work package description.

children.label: Reflect it in the business case update

teach.body: The project board ensures business strategy and objectives are reflected in the business case, and that the project and its management approaches align with the business's ESG commitments. The executive governs in line with strategy, including longer-term environmental, social and economic impacts. Users' sustainability expectations, captured in the project product description, feed the management approaches agreed in initiation.

Ashby Homes, a housing association with a net zero ESG commitment, is retrofitting 300 homes. Project manager Chloe Brennan's business case forecasts tenants' energy bills falling by 25%, with a benefits tolerance of minus 5 percentage points, recorded in the benefits management approach. The sustainability management approach sets an embodied carbon target per home with a 10% tolerance and links it to the net zero goal. When a supplier proposes cheaper insulation that would breach the carbon tolerance, the deviation is escalated.

teach.text: Classic trap: putting tolerances in the wrong place. Benefits tolerance lives in the benefits management approach; sustainability targets and tolerances live in the sustainability management approach. Neither benefits nor quality tolerance appears in a work package description, which carries scope, cost and time.

items: Outcomes and benefits must align with business objectives, which may include ESG goals.
Benefits tolerance: permissible deviation in benefit targets; in the benefits management approach.
Sustainability targets and tolerances: in the sustainability management approach.
The sustainability management approach supports the business case and references ESG goals.
Board: strategy reflected in the business case and alignment with ESG commitments.

summary: You can now explain how the business case aligns to business objectives, including ESG goals. You can also say where benefits tolerance and sustainability targets and tolerances are documented and who keeps the project aligned.

A.why: Benefits tolerance is documented in the benefits management approach (manual 5.2.2).

whyNot.0: The sustainability management approach holds sustainability targets and tolerances.
whyNot.1: Work package descriptions carry scope, cost and time tolerances, not benefits.
whyNot.3: The project product description holds quality expectations and acceptance criteria.

A.q: Which management approach documents the project's sustainability performance targets and tolerances?
A.why: Sustainability performance targets and tolerances are documented in the sustainability management approach, which supports the business case (manual 5.2.2).

whyNot.1: The benefits management approach holds benefits tolerance and benefits reviews.
whyNot.2: The digital and data management approach covers how data and information are handled.
whyNot.3: The communication management approach covers the means and frequency of communication.

options: The limits set on agreed sustainability metrics
The permissible deviation in a product's quality
The limits set on the plan's aggregated risks
The permissible deviation in benefit targets
A.why: Benefits tolerance is the permissible deviation in benefit performance targets before escalation to the next level of management.

B.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. Business objectives may include environmental, social and governance (ESG) goals.
2. Benefits tolerance is agreed in each work package description.
3. The sustainability management approach supports the business case and should reference ESG goals.
4. Sustainability tolerance is the permissible deviation in a product's quality.
B.why: Business objectives may include ESG goals (1), and the sustainability management approach supports the business case and references the organization's ESG goals (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: work package descriptions do not carry benefits tolerance.
whyNot.2: Both are false: benefits tolerance is in the benefits management approach, and sustainability tolerance limits sustainability metrics.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: that describes quality tolerance.

B.q: Which role ensures that the project and its management approaches are aligned with the business's ESG commitments?
B.why: Aligning the project and its approaches to the business's ESG commitments is a project board responsibility.

whyNot.1: The project manager applies the approaches day to day; the board ensures alignment.
whyNot.3: Team managers deliver products within work package tolerances.

B.q: The forecast benefits of a project fall further below target than the benefits tolerance allows. What does this mean?
options: The project manager can absorb it within the stage
It is recorded as a dis-benefit in the business case
It should be escalated to the next management level
The team manager reports it in a checkpoint report
B.why: Tolerance is the deviation allowed before escalation; a forecast beyond benefits tolerance is an exception for the next level of management.

whyNot.0: Deviations within tolerance can be managed locally; this one is beyond tolerance.
whyNot.1: A shortfall against target is not a dis-benefit, which is a measured decline from an outcome.
whyNot.3: Checkpoint reports cover work packages, which carry no benefits tolerance.

C.q: A council's ESG goals include cutting carbon emissions. A depot project sets a carbon target with a permitted margin. Where are the target and margin documented, and what does that product support?
options: Benefits management approach; the project plan
Quality management approach; the business case
Sustainability management approach; the risk register
Sustainability management approach; the business case
C.why: Sustainability targets and tolerances are documented in the sustainability management approach, which supports the business case and should reference ESG goals.

whyNot.0: The benefits management approach holds benefits tolerance, and it supports the business case, not the project plan.
whyNot.1: The quality management approach does not hold sustainability targets.
whyNot.2: The right approach, but it supports the business case; the risk register records risks.

C.q: Which pairing of a tolerance and where it is documented is correct?
C.why: Benefits tolerance is documented in the benefits management approach.

whyNot.0: Sustainability tolerance is in the sustainability management approach.
whyNot.2: Work package descriptions hold scope, cost and time tolerances.
whyNot.3: Quality tolerance comes from acceptance criteria and quality specifications.

C.q: Which statement about aligning the business case to business objectives is correct?
options: Outcomes and benefits should contribute to business objectives
Business objectives are set by the project manager in initiation
Business objectives are the outputs listed in the project brief
Benefits are aligned to the stage plan instead of to objectives
C.why: The outcomes and benefits from the project need to align with and contribute to the business objectives (manual 5.2.2).

whyNot.1: Business objectives come from the organization's strategy, not the project manager.
whyNot.2: Objectives relate to strategy; outputs are the project's products.
whyNot.3: Benefits are aligned to business objectives; stage plans cover delivery.

reteach.title: The household budget with a green pledge
reteach.question: A family renovates its kitchen. It wants lower bills and has also promised to cut its carbon footprint. How would it keep both on track?

blocks.h: Two targets, two margins, two notebooks
blocks.body: The family expects bills to fall by about a fifth and will accept a little less (benefit target and tolerance). It also sets a limit on carbon from new materials (sustainability target and tolerance), tied to its wider pledge (ESG goal). PRINCE2 keeps these in two places: benefits in the benefits management approach, sustainability in the sustainability management approach. If either margin is about to be breached, the decision goes up a level.

blocks.text: Work package descriptions do not carry benefits tolerance: they hold scope, cost and time.

explain.body: Outcomes and benefits must align with and contribute to business objectives. These may include ESG goals.

test.q: According to PRINCE2 7, what may an organization's business objectives include?
options: Product acceptance criteria from the PPD
Work package tolerances set by the PM
Team performance ratings for the year
test.why: Business objectives may include environmental, social and governance (ESG) goals set by the organization (manual 5.2.2).

whyNot.0: Acceptance criteria describe the products, not the organization's objectives.
whyNot.1: Work package tolerances are set by the project manager for team managers.
whyNot.3: Team performance is reviewed for lessons, not set as business objectives.

explain.body: The permissible deviation in benefit performance targets before escalation to the next level. Documented in the benefits management approach.

test.q: Benefits tolerance is the permissible deviation in what?
test.why: Benefits tolerance is the permissible deviation in the benefit performance targets.

whyNot.2: Those are cost and time tolerances.

explain.body: Defines the actions, reviews and controls to ensure the project's sustainability performance targets are achieved. It supports the business case and references ESG goals.

test.q: What does the sustainability management approach define?
options: The reviews that confirm benefits are realized
How data will be stored, secured and retained
How changes to baselines will be controlled
Actions, reviews and controls for sustainability
test.why: It defines the actions, reviews and controls to ensure sustainability performance targets are achieved.

whyNot.0: Benefits reviews are defined in the benefits management approach.
whyNot.1: Data handling is the digital and data management approach.
whyNot.2: Control of changes to baselines is the issue management approach.

explain.body: The business layer sets project tolerances (all seven aspects); the board sets stage tolerances; the project manager sets work package tolerances.

test.q: Which level sets project-level tolerances, including benefits tolerance?
test.why: The business layer sets project tolerances for all seven aspects of performance.

whyNot.1: The project board sets stage tolerances.
whyNot.2: The project manager sets work package tolerances.
whyNot.3: Team managers work within work package tolerances and may set tolerances for team members.
